clue.text: Block of zinc is easily cut into

indicators.note: a block is a solid run cut out of something larger, so the answer is a continuous run of letters in the words that follow

blocks.note: the run starts after the Z of zinc and stops after the E of easily

explanation.surface: A metalworker notes that a slab of zinc is soft enough to cut with ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To incise is to carve or engrave a mark into a surface with a sharp tool.

clue.text: Spoil most of river, clogged off and on

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter, so the river loses its tail
switching off then on again picks every other letter of the word it describes

blocks.note: the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
the second, fourth and sixth letters of clogged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a river has been ruined by repeated blockages.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge a child is to give in to every wish, which is what spoiling one means.

clue.text: Cyprus largely concocted praise

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the island's name is cut short by its last letter
something concocted is cooked up from mixed ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tourist-board praise for Cyprus that is mostly made up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry something up is to talk it up or extol it loudly, a verb phrase for praising.

clue.text: Regular payment of gratuity in dispatch

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the gratuity goes within the dispatch

blocks.note: to dispatch something is to send it
a gratuity is a tip

explanation.surface: An office worker's wage arrives with a bonus tucked into the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary or allowance paid at set intervals, as to a clergyman or student.

clue.text: Picked up kissed Cockney lass that's very sweet

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the answer sounds like the phrase rather than being spelt like it

blocks.note: kissed is necked, and a Cockney drops the H from her, the lass

explanation.surface: An East End romance described as a sweet moment.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for to kiss passionately; the Cockney accent drops initial H, so 'her' becomes 'er.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sugary fluid of flowers, and by extension any drink or thing that is deliciously sweet.

clue.text: Artist wants composer, but not a novelist

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letter named next is taken away from the composer

blocks.note: Sir Edward Elgar, English composer
the letter to be removed
Umberto Eco, Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A painter is after a musician rather than a writer for some project.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Toledo, famous for elongated figures.

clue.text: Earthling's ill nature dealt with

indicators.note: cards dealt out are shuffled first, so these letters are redistributed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's bad temper has been handled at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellurian, from Latin tellus (earth), describes an inhabitant of the planet Earth.

clue.text: Current lead

blocks.note: first meaning: ongoing
second meaning: managing or being in charge

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like electrical terms (current, a lead), but neither is about wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Running means continuing at present and also directing or operating something, so it covers both senses.

clue.text: Check what clot messed up work minimally?

indicators.note: something messed up has been thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager tells someone to look at what an idiot has botched at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like the definition, and fits a clock-watcher, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches the clock is eager for the end of the shift, doing as little as possible meanwhile.

clue.text: Signature of US actress possibly required for date of major operation

blocks.note: Doris Day, the American actress and singer

explanation.surface: An autograph from a Hollywood star is needed for some important appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: D-Day, 6 June 1944, was the date of the Allied landings in Normandy, the largest seaborne invasion.

clue.text: Unexpectedly gaining all oil

indicators.note: an unexpected result comes out differently from what was planned, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speculator suddenly acquires the whole oil supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' looks like the object of gaining, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylang-ylang, also spelt ilang-ilang, is a fragrant essential oil from a tropical tree, used in perfumes.

clue.text: Pass through circuits between earths

indicators.note: something between two things is flanked by them, so the circuits sit inside the pair of earths

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on plugs; two of them
circuits of a track are laps

explanation.surface: An electrician's note about current running through circuits between earth wires.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it goes by, the same as time passing.

clue.text: Heartless brummie bent on first pair of Charlie's Angels

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word goes
bent means twisted out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
on means placed after, so the twisted word follows the opening letters

blocks.note: the first two letters of Charlie
taken as written; one of its two central Ms is removed

explanation.surface: A cruel Birmingham native is obsessed with the trio from the TV show Charlie's Angels.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham. 'Charlie's Angels' reads as one title, but 'Angels' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubim is the plural of cherub, an order of angels in Christian and Jewish tradition.

clue.text: Restoring mostly obscure domestic chore without resistance

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the obscure word is dropped
without means lacking, so the letter for resistance is taken out of the chore

blocks.note: recondite means obscure or little known
pressing clothes is a household task
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone is fixing up a house while avoiding an unclear household job.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconditioning an engine or appliance means overhauling it to good working order again.

clue.text: Spanning two rivers, open stretch

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the word for open reaches around the rivers

blocks.note: overt means done openly
the Exe is a Devon river, and R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bridge crossing two rivers carries an open expanse of road.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert oneself is to push too hard, as in overstretching one's strength.

clue.text: Irresistibly one-sided grovelling — why me getting sacked?

indicators.note: having only one side means an edge has been lost, here the opening letter
sacked as in ransacked, a place turned upside down, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written, then its first letter is lost
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee who just lost their job bemoans their fate in one-sided, self-pitying fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irresistibly one-sided' reads as the definition, but 'one-sided' acts on grovelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelmingly means with a force too great to resist, such as a landslide vote.

clue.text: Stage musical welcomes international actor

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the musical's name holds the letter

blocks.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A West End show takes on a star from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was among the most celebrated English stage and film actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Religious separatist missing number one?

blocks.note: number one is a nursery euphemism for a wee
free of something means without it

explanation.surface: A query whether a breakaway believer lacks a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wee Frees are the Free Church of Scotland, which stayed out of a 1900 union; the wordplay reads it as free of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wee Free is a member of the small Free Church of Scotland that refused to merge, a separatist body.

clue.text: One maltreats half-hearted wife, ever gutted

indicators.note: with half the heart gone, one of the two middle letters is removed
a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: missus is informal for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: An abusive husband's wife is losing heart, eternally broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A misuser is a person who uses something wrongly or treats it badly, the noun for one who maltreats.

clue.text: Limbs and cheek identify body in field?

blocks.note: legs are limbs
lip means cheek, insolence

explanation.surface: A forensic scene: limbs and a face help name a corpse found in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg slip is a fielding position close behind the batsman on the leg side, so the 'body' is a fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder stationed at leg slip is a person standing in the field, hence a body in the field.

clue.text: Measure reservoir in coastal village

blocks.note: to size something is to measure it
a well is a reservoir of water underground

explanation.surface: Someone gauges a water supply in a village by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Sizewell is a village on the Suffolk coast in eastern England, known for its nuclear power stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizewell is a small seaside settlement in Suffolk, so it is a village on the coast.

clue.text: Wild dogs ultimately mean to show no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the dogs is kept
to show no sign means that sign is absent, so it is removed from the word for mean

blocks.note: the final letter of dogs
the mean is the average
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Feral dogs eventually intend to attack without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and wild both describe an untamed, fierce animal or person.

clue.text: Space below centre of driving belt

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept
in a down answer, below means the space word comes underneath, after the kept letter

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters in driving
room means space

explanation.surface: Talk of the room beneath the drive belt in an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving belt' reads as a machine part, but 'belt' alone is the definition, meaning to speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To vroom is to drive off fast with a roaring engine, and to belt along is to go very fast.

clue.text: Absurd scare stops Scottish town's jokes

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so these letters are put into a senseless new order
a stopper plugs a hole, so the shuffled word goes inside the town's name

blocks.note: Wick is a town in Caithness, plus the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ridiculous panic halts a Highland town's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisecracks are smart, flippant remarks made to amuse, which is a kind of joke.

clue.text: Goggles regularly covering left eye up

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the goggles is kept
to cover something is to wrap over it, so the kept letters go round the letter for left

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Goggles
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A swimmer's goggles keep sliding over one eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle someone is to stare at them with obvious desire, which is to eye them up.

clue.text: What a Rechabite getting into wine could become?

definitions.text: What a Rechabite getting into wine could become?

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the pieces before it are placed within the wine

blocks.note: red is a wine
taken as written
a Rechabite is a member of a temperance society, so teetotal, TT

explanation.surface: A wry question about what happens when a sworn abstainer takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a teetotaller drinking wine might end up drunk. Ratted is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller who starts on the wine could get thoroughly drunk, which is what ratted means in British slang.

clue.text: Petition House before judge?

blocks.note: drum is old slang for a house or dwelling
a defendant up before the bench is in court

explanation.surface: A petition is brought before the House of Commons and a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests Parliament, but here it is the slang word for a home; up means appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum up support or business is to canvass actively for it, as petitioning does.
